key_insight: Physician-reviewed, LLM-generated discharge letters improved readability and assessed understandability, with high patient acceptance in a rheumatology feasibility study.
clinical_relevance: Patient-friendly letters may supplement standard discharge information for newly diagnosed rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases, but improved patient comprehension and clinical outcomes remain unproven.
method: Prospective, single-centre, single-arm study enrolling 58 patients; 52 completed follow-up.
GPT models rewrote standard discharge letters; physicians reviewed them before providing both versions to patients.
Evaluation covered review time, discrepancies, information fidelity, readability, understandability and patient feedback.
evidence_signal: Reading Ease improved by 11.4 points and assessed understandability by 10.0 percentage points; review took under five minutes for 43/58 letters, and 44/51 respondents wanted similar letters in future.
watch_item: Unedited drafts contained 11 medical discrepancies across 10/58 letters; 10 discrepancies were corrected before discharge, underscoring the need for physician oversight.
paper_title: LLM-generated patient-friendly discharge letters for newly diagnosed rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases: a prospective feasibility study
